key_insight: Short-range chemical order in high-entropy fluorite oxides initially traps oxygen ions but evolves into interconnected transport networks that enable mobility to exceed that of a random solid solution.
engineering_relevance: Controlling local chemical order could help optimize oxygen transport in minor-actinide-bearing mixed-oxide fuels for advanced fast reactors.
method: Comparison of short-range-ordered and random solid-solution models
Gibbs free-energy minimization and defect analysis
evidence_signal: Simulations across 2000–2800 K reveal a temperature-dependent mobility inversion linked to the evolution from localized oxygen traps to string-like polyhedral networks.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation-based findings without experimental validation, so applicability to irradiated reactor fuels remains to be established.
paper_title: Interplay between high-entropy effects and the superionic transition in fluorite oxides: A liquid-like perspective
